Claude Code on a real project of yours.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
**If your "first project" is a messy active research folder** — multiple
paper drafts, exploratory `.do` files, no README, hardcoded paths — do
the [one-time reorganization walkthrough](reorganize-a-messy-project.qmd)
*first*. Pointing Claude at a chaotic project on day one is the most
common reason colleagues bounce off the tool. Half a day of cleanup is
the difference between Claude being useful and Claude being confusing.
:::

## What this will cover

- **Pick the right project to start with.** A paper draft, a teaching
  repo, or a side project. Not your sensitive replication package.
- **Spend ten minutes letting it read the project.** Ask it to summarize
  what's there. You'll learn what *it* sees, which is roughly what a
  smart RA would see.
- **Pick one annoying task you've been putting off.** "Reformat all my
  tables to use `booktabs`." "Standardize variable names across my
  .do files." "Write a README for this repo." Watch it do that.
- **Read every diff.** This is the habit that matters most.
- **Quit, come back tomorrow.** Notice that it remembers what you were
  doing. That memory is `CLAUDE.md`, covered in
  [Memory, CLAUDE.md, skills](../workflow/memory-and-claude-md.qmd).

*This page is still an outline. If a fuller version would help your work,
email me and I'll prioritize it.*
